steps.note: hero: a single click on slide text opens an inline editing session
steps.caption: Click any text on a slide and you are already editing it.

steps.note: real keystrokes into the slide itself
steps.caption: Real keystrokes replace the headline, live on the slide.
The floating toolbar carries size, weight, colour and alignment.

steps.note: commit the size — the headline re-lays out
steps.caption: Enter commits the size and the slide re-lays out instantly.

steps.note: alignment payoff is relocated from the click — show it full view
steps.caption: Alignment lands on the element you are editing, not the deck.

steps.note: clicking another text run moves the session to it
steps.caption: Click another text run and the session moves with you.

steps.note: bold applies to the run being edited
steps.caption: Bold applies to the run you are in, nothing else.

steps.note: keyboard shortcuts are wired to the same ops
steps.caption: Familiar shortcuts work too: Cmd-B for bold, Cmd-I for italic.

steps.note: escape ends the session; edits stay staged
steps.caption: Escape ends the session; the edits are staged, not saved.

steps.note: closer: the staged edits are written into the slide source file
steps.caption: Save writes every change back into the slide's source file.
